By providing robust theoretical guarantees for initialization and weight dependency that accommodate real-world scenarios (like pruning or correlation induced by training), this work improves the reliability and generalization capability of computationally intensive AI models (like deep Transformers or RNNs) used for forecasting or optimal trade execution. While not a direct alpha strategy, it is crucial for building robust, scalable deep learning trading systems.
title_cn: 关于深度神经网络中雅可比矩阵稳定性的研究
summary_cn: 该研究提供了深度神经网络雅可比矩阵稳定性的普适性理论保证，考虑了稀疏性和依赖性权重。这对于构建金融领域中更稳定、更可靠的深度学习模型至关重要，特别是用于处理复杂时间序列的预测或强化学习模型。通过确保梯度和模型参数的稳定性，可以提高训练效率和泛化能力，间接支撑高频和中频模型的开发。

title: FORGE: Foundational Optimization Representations from Graph Embeddings
summary: Combinatorial optimization problems are ubiquitous in science and engineering. Still, learning-based approaches to accelerate combinatorial optimization often require solving a large number of difficult instances to collect training data, incurring significant computational cost. Existing learning-based methods require training dedicated models for each problem distribution, for each downstream task, severely limiting their scalability and generalization. We introduce Forge: Foundational Optimization Representations from Graph Embeddings, a framework that pre-trains a vector-quantized graph autoencoder on a large, diverse collection of mixed-integer programming (MIP) instances in an unsupervised manner, without relying on optimization solvers or optimal solutions. Vector quantization produces discrete code assignments that serve as a vocabulary for representing optimization instances. We evaluate Forge in both unsupervised and supervised settings. In the unsupervised setting, Forge embeddings effectively cluster unseen instances across problem domains and sizes. In the supervised setting, we fine-tune Forge embeddings and show that a single pre-trained model helps predicting both the integrality gap for cut-generation and variable hints for search guidance across multiple problem and size distributions. In both tasks, we improve the performance of a commercial optimization solver and outperform state-of-the-art learning-based methods. Finally, we open-source our training code, pre-trained Forge weights, and embeddings for multiple MIP distributions to foster further research in representation learning for optimization problems https://skadio.github.io/forge/
core_methodology: The core methodology involves training a vector-quantized graph autoencoder on a large, diverse collection of Mixed-Integer Programming (MIP) instances in an unsupervised manner. This creates 'Foundational Optimization Representations' (embeddings) that capture the structure of optimization problems without needing solver outputs. These embeddings are then used in a supervised setting to predict downstream optimization characteristics (like integrality gap or search guidance hints) for commercial solvers.
data_sources: The data sources are diverse collections of Mixed-Integer Programming (MIP) optimization instances across different problem domains and sizes. This is an abstract representation of optimization problems, not direct financial market data.
alpha_potential: While the paper does not directly propose a trading strategy, its methodology has high relevance for advanced portfolio optimization and resource allocation problems common in quantitative finance. Specifically, portfolio optimization (e.g., maximizing Sharpe ratio under complex constraints, or constructing optimal factor portfolios) often reduces to large-scale MIPs. By using Forge embeddings to quickly represent and then enhance commercial MIP solvers (by providing better initial hints or predicting solution quality), one could significantly speed up the optimization loop for high-frequency portfolio rebalancing or complex asset allocation tasks, which is a tangible competitive advantage in quantitative trading infrastructure.
title_cn: FORGE：基于图嵌入的基础优化表示
summary_cn: 该研究提出了Forge框架，通过对混合整数规划（MIP）实例进行无监督学习，生成优化问题的基础嵌入表示（Graph Embeddings）。该方法可显著提升商业优化求解器的性能，特别是在预测切割生成和搜索指导方面。在量化交易中，此技术可用于加速复杂的投资组合优化、风险预算分配等高频或约束密集型决策过程，带来计算速度优势。

title: Structured Cognitive Loop for Behavioral Intelligence in Large Language Model Agents (Extended Revision: From Behavioral Architecture to Epistemic Accountability)
summary: The central challenge for AI agents is not only performance but accountability. Agents that act through opaque prompt sequences may produce correct outputs, but they provide little basis for verifying why an action was permitted, where an error occurred, or how responsibility should be assigned. This paper presents the Structured Cognitive Loop as an architecture for accountable behavior in large language model agents. SCL separates cognition, memory, control, and action into distinct modules. The language model proposes. External memory preserves verified state. A lightweight controller checks preconditions, prevents redundant actions, and authorizes execution before tools are used. We evaluate SCL against ReAct and common LangChain agent variants across travel planning, conditional email drafting, and constraint guided image generation. Across 360 episodes, SCL achieves 86.3 percent task success compared with 70.5 to 76.8 percent for prompt based baselines. It also improves goal fidelity, reduces redundant tool calls, increases reuse of intermediate state, and lowers unsupported assertions. This extended revision situates SCL within a broader architecture of epistemic accountability. Subsequent extensions integrate context aware Human in the Loop control, Pool Gated Retrieval, and the Horizon Warrant Commitment framework. Together these components define an agent architecture in which the model proposes, structure decides, evidence is warranted before use, and human judgment is embedded in the trace rather than imposed after the fact. The result is a foundation for AI agents whose decisions are not only effective but also authorized, inspectable, and accountable.
core_methodology: The Structured Cognitive Loop (SCL) is an architectural framework for LLM agents that separates cognition, memory, control, and action into distinct modules. It emphasizes verifiable, authorized execution by incorporating a lightweight controller that checks preconditions and authorizes tool use, moving beyond simple prompt-based methods like ReAct.
data_sources: The paper uses general task data (travel planning, email drafting, image generation) for architectural validation, not financial market data. Adaptation would require integrating financial data contexts.
alpha_potential: The SCL architecture itself is not a trading strategy, but it provides a highly robust, accountable, and inspectable framework for building sophisticated AI agents. This is crucial for high-stakes applications like quantitative trading where reliability, traceability, and error prevention (e.g., unauthorized trades, data misuse) are paramount. A structured agent built on SCL could reliably execute complex research pipelines, systematic strategy monitoring, or advanced execution logic where traditional prompt engineering fails due to volatility or complexity.
title_cn: 面向大型语言模型智能体的结构化认知循环：从行为架构到认知问责制（扩展修订版）
summary_cn: 该研究提出的结构化认知循环（SCL）架构，通过模块化设计（认知、记忆、控制、行动）提高了LLM代理的可靠性和可问责性。对于量化交易，SCL提供了一个基础框架，用于构建高可靠性、可审计的交易执行或研究代理，确保每一步决策都经过授权和验证，有效降低复杂策略中的系统性风险。

title: Ultrafast On-chip Online Learning via Spline Locality in Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
summary: Ultrafast online learning is essential for high-frequency systems, such as controls for quantum computing and nuclear fusion, where adaptation must occur on sub-microsecond timescales. Meeting these requirements demands low-latency, fixed-precision computation under strict memory constraints, a regime in which conventional Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs) are both inefficient and numerically unstable. We identify key properties of Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) that align with these constraints. Specifically, we show that: (i) KAN updates exploiting B-spline locality are sparse, enabling superior on-chip resource scaling, and (ii) KANs are inherently robust to fixed-point quantization. By implementing fixed-point online training on Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs), a representative platform for on-chip computation, we demonstrate that KAN-based online learners are significantly more efficient and expressive than MLPs across a range of low-latency and resource-constrained tasks. To our knowledge, this work is the first to demonstrate model-free online learning at sub-microsecond latencies.
core_methodology: The paper proposes leveraging the structural properties of Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs), specifically B-spline locality, to enable ultrafast, sparse, and robust online learning suitable for fixed-precision computation environments like FPGAs. It focuses on achieving sub-microsecond latency updates.
data_sources: The research focuses on demonstrating the learning mechanism using synthetic or low-latency control tasks (like quantum computing controls), not explicit financial market data. Applicable data would be high-frequency time series or market microstructure snapshots.
alpha_potential: While the paper does not detail a trading strategy, the core contribution is the hardware-efficient, ultra-low-latency online learning architecture enabled by KANs. This methodology has high potential for trading applications that require rapid adaptation to changing market regimes or microstructure noise on FPGA platforms, such as ultra-low-latency order routing, dynamic hedging, or high-frequency strategy adaptation where traditional MLPs fail due to computational overhead or instability under quantization.
title_cn: 基于样条局部性的科尔莫果洛夫-阿诺德网络中的超快片上在线学习
summary_cn: 该研究展示了科尔莫果洛夫-阿诺德网络（KANs）在FPGA上实现亚微秒级超快在线学习的潜力。其稀疏更新和固定精度鲁棒性使其成为高频交易系统的理想选择。该方法可用于构建对市场微观结构变化快速适应的低延迟交易策略或模型校准。

title: On the Stability of Nonlinear Dynamics in GD and SGD: Beyond Quadratic Potentials
summary: The dynamical stability of the iterates during training plays a key role in determining the minima obtained by optimization algorithms. For example, stable solutions of gradient descent (GD) correspond to flat minima, which have been associated with favorable features. While prior work often relies on linearization to determine stability, it remains unclear whether linearized dynamics faithfully capture the full nonlinear behavior. Recent work has shown that GD may stably oscillate near a linearly unstable minimum and still converge once the step size decays, indicating that linear analysis can be misleading. In this work, we explicitly study the effect of nonlinear terms. Specifically, we derive an exact criterion for stable oscillations of GD near minima in the multivariate setting. Our condition depends on high-order derivatives, generalizing existing results. Extending the analysis to stochastic gradient descent (SGD), we show that nonlinear dynamics can diverge in expectation even if a single batch is unstable. This implies that stability can be dictated by a single batch that oscillates unstably, rather than an average effect, as linear analysis suggests. Finally, we prove that if all batches are linearly stable, the nonlinear dynamics of SGD are stable in expectation.
core_methodology: This paper analyzes the stability properties of Gradient Descent (GD) and Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) optimization algorithms by explicitly considering nonlinear dynamics beyond simple linearization. It derives conditions for stable oscillations near minima and investigates how non-linear effects influence the convergence and stability of SGD, particularly emphasizing the role of individual batches.
data_sources: The paper primarily deals with theoretical stability analysis of optimization algorithms, not specific financial market data. If applied to trading, the data sources would be the training data used for models (e.g., time series, order book data, fundamental data).
alpha_potential: The direct application is not an alpha signal, but rather optimizing how models (which might generate signals or manage portfolios) are trained. Understanding the stability of SGD is crucial for building robust Machine Learning models for trading. Poor stability can lead to oscillating or diverging models, resulting in suboptimal or fragile trading strategies. Insights on stability could inform hyperparameter tuning (like learning rate schedules) for robust ML-based alpha models.
title_cn: 关于GD和SGD中非线性动力学稳定性的研究：超越二次势能的分析
summary_cn: 该研究深入分析了梯度下降（GD）和随机梯度下降（SGD）的非线性稳定性。虽然不是直接的交易信号，但其结论对构建更稳定的金融机器学习模型至关重要。理解SGD的批次稳定性有助于设计更可靠的优化过程，从而提高基于AI的交易策略的鲁棒性和性能。

title: Detecting High-Potential SMEs with Heterogeneous Graph Neural Networks
summary: Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) constitute 99.9% of U.S. businesses and generate 44% of economic activity, yet systematically identifying high-potential SMEs remains an open challenge. We introduce SME-HGT, a Heterogeneous Graph Transformer framework that predicts which SBIR Phase I awardees will advance to Phase II funding using exclusively public data. We construct a heterogeneous graph with 32,268 company nodes, 124 research topic nodes, and 13 government agency nodes connected by approximately 99,000 edges across three semantic relation types. SME-HGT achieves an AUPRC of 0.621 0.003 on a temporally-split test set, outperforming an MLP baseline (0.590 0.002) and R-GCN (0.608 0.013) across five random seeds. At a screening depth of 100 companies, SME-HGT attains 89.6% precision with a 2.14 lift over random selection. Our temporal evaluation protocol prevents information leakage, and our reliance on public data ensures reproducibility. These results demonstrate that relational structure among firms, research topics, and funding agencies provides meaningful signal for SME potential assessment, with implications for policymakers and early-stage investors.
core_methodology: Utilizes a Heterogeneous Graph Transformer (SME-HGT) model designed to learn relational structures within a heterogeneous graph containing company nodes, research topic nodes, and government agency nodes. The model predicts success probability (Phase I to Phase II funding transition) based on these structural connections.
data_sources: Publicly available data describing Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs), their associated research topics, and government funding agency relationships (specifically SBIR Phase I awards).
alpha_potential: While the paper focuses on predicting future government funding success for SMEs, the underlying methodology demonstrates the value of using Graph Neural Networks to model complex, multi-relational structural data for predictive tasks. This concept is directly transferable to quantitative finance, such as: 1) Predicting future corporate performance or M&A targets based on supply chain/partnership graphs, or 2) Identifying mispriced assets (stocks) based on their structural position within sectoral, innovation, or supplier networks. The performance metrics (AUPRC, lift) suggest a reliable signal extraction capability from structural data.
title_cn: 利用异构图神经网络检测高潜力中小企业
summary_cn: 该研究展示了使用异构图 Transformer (SME-HGT) 从企业、研究主题和政府机构的复杂关系中提取预测信号的能力。在金融领域，该方法可直接应用于构建基于供应链、合作网络或技术路线图的股票筛选模型，通过分析实体间的结构关系来预测公司未来的基本面或股价表现，为因子投资提供新的结构化信号源。

title: ActMem: Bridging the Gap Between Memory Retrieval and Reasoning in LLM Agents
summary: Memory management is essential for LLM agents in long-term interactions. Current memory frameworks typically treat agents as passive ``recorders'' and retrieve information without understanding its deeper implications. They may fail in scenarios requiring reasoning and complex decision-making. To bridge this critical gap, we propose a novel actionable memory framework called ActMem that integrates memory retrieval with active causal reasoning. ActMem transforms unstructured dialogue history into a structured causal and semantic graph. By leveraging counterfactual reasoning and commonsense completion, it enables agents to deduce implicit constraints and resolve potential conflicts between past states and current intentions. Furthermore, we introduce a comprehensive dataset ActMemEval to evaluate agent reasoning capabilities in logic-driven scenarios, moving beyond the fact-retrieval focus of existing memory benchmarks. Experiments demonstrate that ActMem significantly outperforms baselines in handling complex, memory-dependent tasks, paving the way for more consistent and reliable intelligent assistants.
core_methodology: ActMem introduces an actionable memory framework integrating memory retrieval with active causal reasoning. It transforms unstructured dialogue history into a structured causal and semantic graph, utilizing counterfactual reasoning and commonsense completion to deduce implicit constraints and resolve conflicts between past states and intentions.
data_sources: The abstract focuses on improving LLM agent reasoning using dialogue history as input, primarily evaluating logic-driven scenarios (ActMemEval dataset). For quant finance, this implies using structured logs of past trading decisions, market states, or analytical discussions as input for causal reasoning.
alpha_potential: While the paper focuses on general AI agents, the core mechanism—causal and semantic graph construction from history to inform complex, multi-step decision-making—is highly valuable for sophisticated trading agents. It could significantly enhance sequential execution strategies, portfolio management adjustments based on contextual history, or complex trade sequencing where implicit constraints derived from past actions must be respected. For instance, an agent managing complex derivatives or multi-asset allocation over long periods needs to avoid actions that contradict inferred long-term objectives or previous successful/failed patterns.
title_cn: ActMem：弥合LLM智能体中记忆检索与推理之间的鸿沟
summary_cn: ActMem提出一种可操作的记忆框架，通过将历史信息转化为因果语义图，增强LLM智能体的主动因果推理能力。该技术能帮助交易智能体更好地处理涉及长期交互和复杂决策的场景，例如在执行复杂的、需要上下文一致性的多步骤交易策略时，避免与历史约束冲突的决策，从而提高策略的可靠性和一致性。

title: TopBench: A Benchmark for Implicit Predictive Reasoning in Tabular Question Answering
summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) have advanced Table Question Answering, where most queries can be answered by extracting information or simple aggregation. However, a common class of real-world queries is implicitly predictive, requiring the inference of unobserved answers from historical patterns rather than mere retrieval. These queries introduce two challenges: recognizing latent intent and reliable predictive reasoning over massive tables. To assess LLMs in such Tabular questiOn answering with implicit Prediction tasks, we introduce TopBench, a benchmark consisting of 779 samples across four sub-tasks, ranging from single-point prediction to decision making, treatment effect analysis, and complex filtering, requiring models to generate outputs spanning reasoning text and structured tables. We evaluate diverse models under both text-based and agentic workflows. Experiments reveal that current models often struggle with intent recognition, defaulting to just lookups. Deeper analysis identifies that accurate intent disambiguation serves as the prerequisite for leading these predictive behaviors. Furthermore, elevating the upper bound of prediction precision requires the integration of more sophisticated modeling or reasoning capabilities.
core_methodology: The core methodology involves benchmarks (TopBench) designed to test Large Language Models (LLMs) on implicit predictive reasoning tasks over tabular data, moving beyond simple retrieval or aggregation. This includes tasks like single-point prediction, decision-making, and treatment effect analysis based on historical patterns.
data_sources: Tabular data representing historical patterns, akin to structured financial records, time series data, or fundamental data tables used in quantitative analysis.
alpha_potential: While the paper does not propose a trading strategy, it directly targets the capability of LLMs to perform *implicit predictive reasoning* over structured data. In finance, this is highly relevant for tasks like predicting future factor exposures, inferring optimal portfolio rebalancing decisions under complex constraints, or performing causal inference (treatment effect analysis, e.g., impact of a specific corporate action). Improving LLM's ability to recognize latent intent and reason probabilistically over tables is a necessary step for building advanced, data-driven quantitative agents, moving them beyond simple lookups to genuine forecasting and decision support.
title_cn: TopBench：面向表格问答中隐式预测推理的基准测试
summary_cn: 该研究介绍了TopBench，一个用于评估大语言模型（LLMs）在表格数据上执行隐式预测推理（如推断未来趋势、决策支持）的能力的基准。这对于量化交易系统具有潜在价值，因为它旨在提升LLM超越简单信息检索，通过分析历史模式进行复杂预测和决策制定的能力，这是构建高级量化智能体的关键。”

title: Multi-Agent Systems are Mixtures of Experts: Who Becomes an Influencer?
summary: The effectiveness of multi-agent LLM deliberation depends not only on the agents' individual predictions, but also on how they communicate and collaborate. We study this mechanism through the lens of Friedkin-Johnsen (FJ) opinion dynamics, a tractable model for analyzing stubbornness, influence, and opinion change in multi-agent systems that captures empirically observed deliberation patterns. We show that the FJ parameters are input-dependent, turning multi-agent deliberation into a mixture of experts. This perspective implies that multi-agent systems can outperform single agents and static ensembles when routing reflects agent competence. Since competence is latent in practice, we analyze how influence is established through observable proxies: agents' self-assessed confidence, their perceived confidence, and initial alignment with other agents' views.
core_methodology: The paper analyzes multi-agent deliberation using the Friedkin-Johnsen (FJ) opinion dynamics model. It frames the process as a Mixture of Experts (MoE) setup, where agent influence (competence) is driven by observable proxies like self-assessed confidence, perceived confidence, and initial alignment. The core mechanism involves routing decisions based on inferred agent competence within a collaborative AI framework.
data_sources: The primary data sources involve agent communication, self-reported confidence metrics, and observed opinion dynamics within the multi-agent system. While not traditional financial market data, the framework is applicable to data generated by AI agents producing market predictions or trade signals.
alpha_potential: The framework suggests that structured deliberation among specialized LLM agents (a form of AI ensemble) can outperform static or simple ensembles if the system effectively routes decisions based on inferred agent 'competence' (influence). This directly applies to building robust, state-of-the-art AI trading systems where multiple agents synthesize information. The key alpha source lies in optimally weighting or selecting signals from diverse opinionated or specialized AI models, moving beyond simple averaging to dynamic routing based on inferred reliability.
title_cn: 多智能体系统即专家混合模型：谁将成为影响力人物？
summary_cn: 该研究将多智能体决策视为专家混合模型（MoE），利用Friedkin-Johnsen模型分析智能体间的实际影响力和意见动态。这为构建更鲁棒的AI交易系统提供了理论基础，通过根据智能体的隐含能力（如信心度）动态路由决策，有望超越静态或简单集成模型，从而增强市场预测的准确性和交易决策的效率。

title: DN-Hypo-Pipeline: An AI-Driven Workflow for Hypothesis Generation via Large Language Models and Scientific Explanations
summary: A scientific hypothesis is the first step in research and undergoes experimental validation, yet it also reflects a deep understanding of and reasoning about scientific phenomena. We introduce DN-Hypo-Pipeline, an AI-powered workflow based on large language models, designed to support structured scientific thinking and hypothesis generation by leveraging scientific explanations as prior knowledge. This pipeline assists researchers in deriving novel hypotheses from existing literature. Given the explanandum (i.e., the conclusion) of a research paper, it identifies underlying laws, theories, and principles, and reconstructs a new, yet-to-be-verified explanation for the observed phenomenon. We evaluated DN-Hypo-Pipeline in the field of data science modeling using three highly cited papers. Statistical inference, supported by both LLM-as-judge assessment and human expert evaluation, demonstrates that our pipeline is more effective than direct generation methods. Additionally, we validated the two highest-scoring generated hypotheses by developing corresponding novel algorithms, which outperformed the baseline models presented in the original papers. Beyond application in data science, DN-Hypo-Pipeline provides a theoretical framework that not only encompasses theory-guided data science modeling methods but also reveals a more fundamental structure of the modeling process. Moreover, this approach is essentially a generalization of theory-guided modeling, offering potential for extension to other domains and across a broader range of scientific disciplines.
core_methodology: The DN-Hypo-Pipeline uses Large Language Models (LLMs) to reverse-engineer scientific explanations and established principles from existing research (the explanandum, or conclusion) to generate novel, verifiable hypotheses. It leverages scientific explanations as structured prior knowledge to guide the LLM's output, rather than relying solely on direct generation.
data_sources: The abstract indicates evaluation on data science modeling papers, suggesting a reliance on structured scientific literature and conclusions as input data. In a financial context, this would involve academic papers, regulatory filings, or internal research reports.
alpha_potential: The direct application is not a trading strategy, but a meta-strategy framework. It provides a structured method for generating novel, high-potential algorithmic trading hypotheses by systematically dissecting existing knowledge (e.g., established economic theories or successful past algorithms) and proposing verifiable, novel extensions or alternative models. The abstract notes that generated hypotheses led to superior novel algorithms in a validation set, suggesting strong potential for creating performance-enhancing algorithmic components.
title_cn: 利用大型语言模型和科学解释进行假设生成的人工智能驱动工作流：DN-Hypo-Pipeline
summary_cn: DN-Hypo-Pipeline是一个利用大型语言模型（LLM）和既有科学解释来系统性地生成新的交易假设的框架。它通过反向推导现有结论背后的原理，辅助量化研究人员发现新的、可验证的算法构建思路。该方法有望加速因子挖掘和模型创新，通过结构化地探索知识边界来提高策略的超额收益潜力。

title: DiPOD: Diffusion Policy Optimization without Drifting Apart
summary: RL post-training has become increasingly pivotal for improving diffusion policies, but existing diffusion policy-gradient methods are often unstable and cannot achieve reliable policy improvement. We identify the cause as the double-drift phenomenon: optimizing a variational surrogate can let the ELBO separate from the true log-likelihood, which then makes the resulting proxy policy gradient misaligned with the true policy gradient of expected return. We propose \textbf{DiPOD}, a diffusion policy optimization framework that maintains tight-bound behavior throughout training by interleaving self-distillation with policy-improving gradient updates. This leads to a simple and practical algorithm: augmenting each diffusion policy-gradient update with an on-policy ELBO regularizer. Across diffusion language model post-training and continuous-control diffusion policies, DiPOD substantially stabilizes training and reaches higher rewards than previous methods.
core_methodology: DiPOD is a Diffusion Policy Optimization framework that stabilizes training for diffusion policies by mitigating the 'double-drift' phenomenon. It achieves this by interleaving self-distillation with policy-improving gradient updates, specifically by augmenting policy-gradient updates with an on-policy Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO) regularizer.
data_sources: The paper demonstrates efficacy on Diffusion Language Models (used here for policy generation) and continuous-control diffusion policies. For finance, this implies application to high-dimensional sequential decision-making tasks, likely involving time-series data, order book dynamics, or portfolio allocation paths.
alpha_potential: The core value lies in improving the stability and performance of high-capacity Reinforcement Learning (RL) agents parameterized by diffusion models. Diffusion models are powerful generative models capable of capturing complex, multi-modal distributions over actions or future states (e.g., optimal trading paths). DiPOD makes these powerful models reliably trainable for complex trading tasks like optimal execution or dynamic portfolio management, where standard RL often fails due to instability.
title_cn: DiPOD：无漂移扩散策略优化
summary_cn: DiPOD提出了一种用于稳定和提升扩散策略优化的新框架，通过引入ELBO正则化稳定了基于扩散模型的强化学习训练。这对于构建使用扩散模型生成复杂、高维交易策略（如动态资产配置或最优执行路径）的AI交易代理至关重要，有望显著提高这些复杂策略的性能和可靠性。

title: GRACE-DS: a Guarded Reward-guided Agent Correction Environment in Data Science
summary: We introduce GRACE-DS, a Guarded Reward-guided Agent Correction Environment in Data Science for pre-deployment evaluation of LLM-powered AutoML agents. GRACE-DS is a set of evaluation metrics in an isolated environment that can be applied to tabular ML tasks specific to a particular organization. It exposes agents to realistic workflow stages, from planning and data inspection through feature engineering, model development, validation, and code repair to final submission, while hidden executable validators measure not only final predictive performance but also leakage avoidance, reproducibility, protocol validity, correction behavior, and reward alignment. The strongest structured regime, flexible iterative interaction (our approach), achieves higher end-to-end normalized hidden-test quality than single-shot generation, unstructured interaction, and restart-based baselines, while also improving protocol-valid completion. Validated across more than 7,000 episodes, these results establish GRACE-DS as a robust platform for assessing the capacity of LLM-based AutoML agents to execute machine learning workflows under production-like conditions and in accordance with organization-specific requirements.
core_methodology: The core methodology introduces GRACE-DS, an evaluation environment for LLM-powered AutoML agents. It focuses on creating a structured, guarded, and reward-guided system to assess the agents' ability to execute the entire ML workflow (planning, data inspection, feature engineering, modeling, validation, code repair) under realistic, organization-specific constraints (like leakage avoidance and reproducibility). The approach emphasizes iterative interaction over single-shot generation for better workflow completion and quality.
data_sources: The environment is designed for tabular ML tasks typical in data science, applied to an organization's specific datasets. In a finance context, this would imply internal time-series or cross-sectional datasets (e.g., stock features, alternative data, order book snapshots).
alpha_potential: The direct alpha potential is low, as the paper describes a *meta-system* for evaluating AutoML agents, not a trading strategy itself. However, the indirect potential is high: successfully deploying LLM agents capable of robust, self-correcting ML workflow generation directly translates to faster, more reliable development and deployment of quantitative trading strategies. It reduces human intervention and ensures adherence to internal production rules (like avoiding lookahead bias or data leakage), which are critical challenges in high-frequency and signal research.
title_cn: GRACE-DS：一个用于数据科学中由奖励引导的代理纠错环境
summary_cn: 该论文开发了一个评估框架（GRACE-DS），用于测试LLM驱动的AutoML智能体在表格数据任务中的端到端执行能力。虽然不是直接的阿尔法策略，但该框架能确保量化团队开发的模型在数据处理、特征工程和验证阶段，严格遵守组织特定的生产要求（如避免数据泄露和提高可复现性）。这极大地加速和保障了量化策略的稳定部署和迭代。

title: Unreduced Persistence Diagrams for Topological Machine Learning
summary: Supervised machine learning pipelines trained on features derived from persistent homology have been experimentally observed to ignore much of the information contained in a persistence diagram. Computing persistence diagrams is often the most computationally demanding step in such a pipeline, however. To explore this dynamic, we introduce several methods to generate topological feature vectors from unreduced boundary matrices and investigate their theoretical and computational properties. We compared the performance of pipelines trained on vectorizations of unreduced PDs to vectorizations of fully-reduced PDs across several data and task types. Our results indicate that models trained on PDs built from unreduced diagrams can perform on par and even outperform those trained on fully-reduced diagrams on some tasks. We also benchmarked the computational performance of an algorithm for computing unreduced diagrams, which was implemented as a heavily modified version of Ripser. These computations are parallelizable and required an order of magnitude less memory on average compared to computing full persistence diagrams. Our results suggest that machine learning pipelines which incorporate topology-based features may benefit in terms of computational cost and performance by utilizing information contained in unreduced boundary matrices.
core_methodology: The paper introduces novel methods to generate topological feature vectors directly from unreduced boundary matrices in persistent homology, bypassing the need for full Persistence Diagrams (PDs). It compares the performance and computational efficiency of these 'unreduced PD' features against traditional, fully-reduced features in supervised machine learning pipelines.
data_sources: The paper uses general 'data and task types' for benchmarking topological machine learning performance, implying application to generic structured or time-series data, which would need to be financial datasets in a trading context (e.g., price series, order book data, market graphs).
alpha_potential: Topological Data Analysis (TDA), specifically persistent homology, can be used to summarize complex, high-dimensional market dynamics (like multivariate correlations, market regime shapes, or network structure) into stable topological features. The practical breakthrough here is computational efficiency: if generating these topological features can be made significantly faster (order of magnitude less memory, faster computation), using TDA for high-speed trading applications or incorporating more complex structures becomes feasible. This could potentially allow for novel, structure-based alpha signals derived from the shape of market data distributions or cross-asset relationships.
title_cn: 用于拓扑机器学习的非简化持久性图
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种新的拓扑数据分析特征提取方法，可以直接从边界矩阵生成特征向量，避免了计算高成本的完整持久性图。在交易中，这意味着可以更快、占用更少内存地提取市场数据的拓扑结构信息，从而有望应用于高频或需要复杂结构分析的量化策略，提升信号提取的效率和性能。

title: Everywhere Valid Bounds on False Discovery Proportions in Conformal Inference
summary: Modern applications of conformal inference to multiple testing problems, such as outlier detection and candidate selection, often involve selecting test samples whose conformal p-values fall below a threshold. The quality of such methods is often measured by the false discovery proportion (FDP), defined as the fraction of incorrect selections. Existing approaches typically control the expected value of the FDP, using methods such as the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure. This approach fails to provide high-probability bounds on the realized false discovery proportion and invalidates statistical guarantees if the rejection threshold is selected after inspecting the data. This paper establishes finite-sample, distribution-free upper bounds on the FDP that hold simultaneously over all possible rejection thresholds, enabling arbitrary post hoc selection of the threshold. Simultaneous validity is achieved by constructing a high-probability envelope for the empirical distribution function of null conformal p-values by sampling from their joint distribution. Furthermore, our framework allows practitioners to modulate the envelope's shape, thereby producing tight bounds in rejection regions of primary interest. We use this flexible approach to derive simultaneous FDP upper bounds for both outlier detection and conformal selection. We demonstrate through synthetic and real-data experiments that the resulting bounds are both valid and substantially less conservative than those derived from existing approaches.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a novel framework for Conformal Inference that provides finite-sample, distribution-free upper bounds on the False Discovery Proportion (FDP). It achieves simultaneous validity over all possible rejection thresholds by constructing a high-probability envelope using the joint distribution of null conformal p-values. This allows for flexible threshold selection post-data inspection.
data_sources: The core methodology focuses on methodological improvements within statistical testing (conformal inference and multiple hypothesis testing). Application data is implied to be any dataset where hypothesis testing or outlier/candidate selection is performed, potentially including financial time series or feature importance rankings.
alpha_potential: While not a direct trading strategy, the methodology offers significant value in rigorous statistical validation for feature selection, hyperparameter tuning, and model validation workflows in quantitative trading. Specifically, it can provide stronger, distribution-free guarantees on the reliability of selected features or trading signals, reducing the risk associated with data snooping or p-hacking when setting selection thresholds post-hoc. This ensures that when a set of candidate signals is chosen for backtesting, the observed performance (or error rate) is statistically sound with high probability, improving the robustness of signal construction pipelines.
title_cn: 共形推断中关于错误发现比例的普遍有效界限
summary_cn: 该研究提出了共形推断的创新方法，可提供有限样本、无分布的错误发现比例（FDP）高概率上界。这对于量化交易中特征选择、信号筛选和模型验证至关重要，因为它能够在事后灵活选择阈值时，提供比传统方法更稳健、保守性更低的统计有效性保证，有效控制策略中的误报风险。

title: Data-driven sparse identification of governing PDEs via knockoff filters and multi-criteria trade-offs
summary: We propose KO-PDE-IDENT, a data-driven framework for identifying parsimonious partial differential equations (PDEs) with false discovery rate (FDR) control. PDE discovery from noisy observations is often hindered by extreme multicollinearity among candidate terms, which causes typical sparse-regression methods to select spurious terms. To address this problem, KO-PDE-IDENT initially mines a support set of potential candidate terms via model-X knockoff filters with finite-sample FDR control, then refines and ranks the surviving PDE alternatives. The framework integrates three components. First, knockoff feature statistics are constructed by coupling $\ell_{0}$-constrained adaptive best-subset selection with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), yielding an effective and computationally efficient difference statistic. Second, a recursive feature elimination (RFE) procedure removes terms whose marginal contributions are dispensable and assesses statistical necessity through knockoff-perturbed hypothesis testing. Third, the final model selection is formulated as a multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) problem, where the optimal governing equation is the alternative that best balances a wide range of criteria such as predictive accuracy, model complexity and coefficient uncertainty. We evaluate KO-PDE-IDENT on five canonical PDEs under severe noise corruption. Empirical results show that our framework can exactly recover the true PDE structure, eliminating false discoveries while retaining all true underlying terms, with low coefficient estimation error.
core_methodology: The paper introduces KO-PDE-IDENT, a framework for discovering sparse Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) from noisy data. It uses Model-X knockoff filters for feature selection with False Discovery Rate (FDR) control to handle multicollinearity, combined with SHAP values. The process includes recursive feature elimination (RFE) and a final model selection step using Multi-Criteria Decision Making (MCDM) to balance accuracy, complexity, and uncertainty.
data_sources: The methodology is designed for noisy observational data where the underlying generating process is governed by PDEs. In finance, this could apply to time-series data exhibiting complex dynamics, such as high-frequency limit order book data, volatility surfaces, or energy/commodity futures curves.
alpha_potential: While the paper focuses on canonical PDEs from physics, the core contribution is a robust method for identifying parsimonious, interpretable governing equations from noisy financial time-series data. In quantitative finance, this is highly valuable for: 1) **Model Discovery:** Discovering latent factor models or nonlinear relationships in asset returns or volatility that are better represented by differential equations than standard statistical models. 2) **Risk Modeling:** Creating interpretable, sparse models for systemic risk or derivative pricing dynamics. The FDR control addresses the noise and spurious correlation common in financial data, making the discovered structures potentially more robust for strategy development.
title_cn: 基于Knockoff滤波器和多准则权衡的数据驱动控制偏微分方程稀疏识别
summary_cn: 该框架KO-PDE-IDENT提供了一种从高噪声观测数据中稳健识别稀疏控制PDE的有效方法，通过使用Knockoff滤波器控制错误发现率（FDR）。在量化交易中，此技术可用于发现衍生品定价、波动率动态或宏观经济时间序列背后的潜在、简洁且可解释的数学结构，从而构建更具鲁棒性的因子模型或风险模型。

title: Knockoffs-based False Discovery Rate Control and Simplification for Deep Neural Networks
summary: The deep neural network is a widely used framework in machine learning that has been widely applied in various fields. However, deep neural networks often involve a large number of parameters and inputs, many of which may be irrelevant to the goal or true output. These parameters and input variables not only increase computational complexity, but also contribute to additional computational cost. One solution to this problem is knockoff methods, which have proven successful in controlling false discovery rates in high-dimensional regression. Building on the knockoff methods and using the regularised neural network, this paper proposes three variable screening methods under the condition of controlling false discovery rates: one layer filter, multiple layers filter, and variable weight aggregation filter. In comparison with existing algorithms, we find that our algorithms show satisfactory performance.
core_methodology: The paper introduces three variable screening methods (one layer filter, multiple layers filter, and variable weight aggregation filter) based on knockoff methods, specifically tailored for regularized deep neural networks. The primary goal is to control the False Discovery Rate (FDR) when selecting relevant input features or internal parameters.
data_sources: While the abstract discusses general DNN applications, the methodology is designed for high-dimensional data typical in quantitative finance, such as large sets of fundamental data, macroeconomic indicators, time-series features, or high-frequency microstructure data.
alpha_potential: The core practical value lies in feature selection and model simplification for deep learning models used in trading. By controlling the FDR during feature screening, this method can select the most predictive inputs for DNN-based alpha models, reducing computational overhead and improving interpretability while ensuring the integrity of selected features (i.e., minimizing false signals chosen as predictors). This directly supports building robust, parsimonious alpha factors.
title_cn: 基于Knockoffs的深度神经网络的错误发现率控制与简化
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种基于Knockoff方法的新型变量筛选技术，用于深度神经网络的特征选择，同时严格控制错误发现率（FDR）。这对于量化交易中处理高维复杂模型至关重要，因为它能有效识别出对预测目标真正有贡献的输入特征，从而简化模型结构、降低计算成本，并提高模型预测的可靠性和稳健性。

title: DRIFT: Refining Instruction Data via On-Policy Data Attribution
summary: Optimizing the training data distribution for Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) dictates the capability of Large Language Models (LLMs). While existing data curation methods excel at accelerating training under constrained budgets, they are less suited to elevating the capability upper bound. The challenge here is no longer to identify a smaller subset that preserves performance, but to refine the data distribution toward instances most capable of improving the final model. To address this problem, we explore instance-level data attribution using Influence Functions (IF). We identify that standard IF formulations struggle in this setting due to two structural limitations: a proximity gap caused by off-policy validation targets, and a severe bias towards gradient norm. We propose DRIFT (Data Refinement via On-Policy Influence Functions for Supervised Fine-Tuning). Instead of relying on external reference data, DRIFT utilizes the model's on-policy rollouts as validation targets, which empirically minimizes the parameter proximity gap and better aligns with the local neighborhood assumption of IF. It further applies signed weighting based on trajectory correctness and debiases influence scores against the gradient hacking issue, allowing a small set of validation queries to act as reliable anchors for attributing the full dataset. Experiments on 7B-parameter instruction and reasoning models show that DRIFT consistently raises the performance ceiling on both, outperforming existing data curation baselines.
core_methodology: The paper introduces DRIFT, a novel data curation method for Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) of LLMs. It refines training data distribution by leveraging Influence Functions (IF) applied to 'on-policy' validation targets (the model's own rollouts) rather than external data. It addresses limitations of standard IFs, such as the proximity gap and gradient norm bias, by using signed weighting and debiasing techniques to identify data instances that most effectively improve the model's capability ceiling.
data_sources: The methodology focuses on improving the quality of instruction and reasoning data used for fine-tuning large language models (LLMs). While the abstract does not specify financial market data, the technique is applicable to refining datasets of human-generated trading rationales, model-generated market analysis, or labeled financial examples.
alpha_potential: The primary potential for quantitative trading lies in enhancing LLMs designed for financial tasks. By improving the SFT process, DRIFT can lead to more capable LLMs for: 1) generating higher-quality trading signals from unstructured data (news, reports, transcripts); 2) developing more robust AI agents capable of complex decision-making; and 3) refining backtesting and simulation environments by creating better synthetic data or evaluating strategy logic. Improving the 'capability upper bound' of financial LLMs is a direct lever for better alpha generation.
title_cn: DRIFT：通过策略内数据归因精炼指令数据
summary_cn: 该研究提出DRIFT方法，利用模型自身的“策略内”输出来精炼LLM的SFT训练数据，克服了传统数据归因方法的局限。该技术可用于优化用于金融市场分析、信号生成和交易决策的专业LLM，从而提高模型性能上限，间接提升量化策略的Alpha生成能力。

title: Bounded Context Management for Tabular Foundation Models on Stream Learning
summary: Tabular stream learning requires predictions on sequentially arriving examples under distribution shift. While standard methods adapt by updating model states, tabular foundation models (TFMs) make predictions conditioned on a labeled context in an in-context manner, making them a natural alternative for stream learning. This shifts the challenge from how to update the model to how to manage the context. We propose a future information view that yields three practical requirements for context management: preserve recent examples, retain uncertain examples, and remove redundant examples. We instantiate these requirements as CURE (Context management via Uncertainty-aware admission and Redundancy aware Eviction), a context-managing policy with entropy-gated admission and redundancy-aware eviction. Across seven streams, CURE shows up to 27.0% relative improvement over classical stream learners, remains robust across multiple TFM backbones, and ranks first among other policy variants. Code and datasets are available at https://github.com/morcellinus/CURE-ICML-FMSD.
core_methodology: The paper introduces CURE (Context management via Uncertainty-aware admission and Redundancy aware Eviction), a policy for managing the context window of Tabular Foundation Models (TFMs) operating in a stream learning setting. It prioritizes preserving recent and uncertain examples while actively removing redundant ones using entropy-gated admission and redundancy-aware eviction to handle distribution shifts in sequential data.
data_sources: The abstract specifies 'tabular data streams' and evaluation across 'seven streams,' which typically refers to sequential, structured datasets, potentially mimicking transactional or time-series data but applied here to general tabular learning tasks.
alpha_potential: The core value lies in enabling Transformer-based/Foundation Models (which excel at complex feature interactions) to effectively process high-frequency, sequentially arriving financial time-series data while adapting to non-stationarity (distribution shift). In finance, this could stabilize predictions for factor models, regime detection, or high-frequency order book modeling where context management is critical for adapting to evolving market conditions without full retraining.
title_cn: 面向流学习的表格型基础模型的有界上下文管理
summary_cn: 该研究提出了CURE策略，用于管理面向流学习的表格型基础模型（TFM）的上下文窗口。通过智能地保留近期和不确定性样本，并清除冗余信息，CURE解决了金融时间序列数据中常见的分布漂移问题。这使得强大的TFM架构能更稳定地应用于高频预测、因子动态调整或市场微观结构分析等场景，提供了处理非平稳金融流数据的有效机制。

title: GrapNet: A Programmable Dynamic-Architecture Neural Graph Substrate
summary: Programmability is a missing first-class interface in fixed-tensor neural networks: editing a relation, freezing a subgraph, auditing a local function, or changing the execution backend should be an operation on the neural program rather than ad-hoc parameter surgery. GrapNet studies this graph-as-network setting. The graph is the architecture and executable program, not an input data graph. Each compute node owns its next-layer child references and a trainable allocation vector aligned with those references; deleting a relation physically removes both the child reference and the corresponding allocation coordinate. Structural rules and execution policies live outside the node core, so the same child-owned graph can be grown, frozen, structurally edited, grouped into trainable family blocks, routed by attention over active relations, or lowered to dense snapshots after topology stabilizes. GrapNet composes with conventional modules through a vector-valued parent interface: dense layers, CNN encoders, ResNet feature extractors, attention blocks, and transformer representations can all feed one sensory GrapNode per coordinate. The evaluation is organized as a programmability stress suite rather than as a new replay benchmark. In a matched ten-seed Split Fashion-MNIST study, a plastic GrapNet+ER head reaches 63.16 percent seen-class accuracy versus 51.08 percent for a parameter-larger dense MLP+ER under the same seen-class loss and replay memory, with paired delta 12.08 points and p=1.3e-5. On Split CIFAR-10 with a frozen ImageNet ResNet-18 encoder, the same substrate improves the online head over MLP-256 by 3.81 points, with p=0.0026. These results support GrapNet as an editable neural graph substrate whose core value is structural programmability with faithful execution views.
core_methodology: GrapNet introduces a dynamic-architecture neural graph substrate where the graph structure itself is programmable and executable, rather than fixed. It allows for on-the-fly editing of relations, freezing subgraphs, and flexible execution routing, contrasting with standard fixed-tensor networks. Computation is structured around 'GrapNodes' that manage child layer references and allocation vectors.
data_sources: The paper primarily uses standard image datasets (Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10) for architectural evaluation, not financial data. However, the *architecture* is adaptable to any structured data, including financial time series or market graphs.
alpha_potential: While the paper focuses on image classification benchmarks, the core innovation—a highly adaptable and editable neural architecture—has significant potential for complex financial modeling. Traditional fixed-topology models struggle to adapt to regime shifts or rapidly evolving market structures. GrapNet's programmability could allow for dynamically restructuring neural networks to reflect changing market relationships (e.g., factor breakdowns, sector connectivity) in real-time, potentially leading to more robust execution or better adaptation in Reinforcement Learning trading agents.
title_cn: GrapNet：一种可编程的动态架构神经图基底
summary_cn: GrapNet提出了一种新型神经计算架构，其中图结构本身是可编程和可编辑的。虽然本文在图像任务上进行了验证，但其核心价值在于动态适应性。这对于构建能实时调整内部结构以应对市场制度切换或因子关系变化的金融模型具有潜在价值，可用于更灵活的强化学习或复杂关系建模。

title: GraphPO: Graph-based Policy Optimization for Reasoning Models
summary: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) has become a standard paradigm for enhancing the capability of large reasoning models. RLVR typically samples responses independently and optimizes the policy using from final answers. This paradigm has two limitations. First, independently responses often contain similar intermediate reasoning steps, causing redundant exploration and wasted computation. Second, sparse final-answer rewards make it hard to identify useful steps. Tree-based methods partly address this problem by sharing prefixes and comparing branches from the same prefix to provide fine-grained signals. However, tree branches are still expanded independently. When different branches reach similar reasoning states, they cannot share information and repeat similar exploration. Moreover, tree-based methods ignore such dispersion and only perform local comparisons within separate branches, which can lead to higher variance in advantage estimation. To address this challenge, we propose GraphPO (Graph-based Policy Optimization), a novel RL framework that represents rollouts as a directed acyclic graph, with reasoning steps as edges and semantic states summarized from the reasoning paths as nodes. GraphPO merges semantically equivalent reasoning paths into equivalence classes, allowing them to share suffixes and reallocating budget away from redundant expansions to diverse exploration. Furthermore, we assign efficiency advantages to incoming edges and correctness advantages to outgoing edges, thereby improving inference efficiency while deriving process supervision from outcome. Theory shows that GraphPO reduces advantage-estimation variance and enhances reasoning efficiency. Experiments on three LLMs across reasoning and agentic search benchmarks show that GraphPO consistently outperforms chain- and tree-based baselines with the same token budgets or response budgets.
core_methodology: GraphPO (Graph-based Policy Optimization) is a novel Reinforcement Learning framework designed for reasoning models. It represents rollouts as a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG), where nodes are semantically summarized states and edges are reasoning steps. It merges semantically equivalent reasoning paths (nodes) into equivalence classes, allowing for shared suffixes and improved exploration efficiency by avoiding redundant computation in similar reasoning states. It uses efficiency and correctness advantages assigned to edges to guide policy updates.
data_sources: The paper focuses on benchmark datasets for reasoning tasks (e.g., LLM benchmarks), not explicit financial data. However, the methodology is transferrable to sequential decision-making problems in finance.
alpha_potential: While the paper's focus is on improving Large Language Model (LLM) reasoning capabilities, the underlying Graph-based Policy Optimization (GraphPO) methodology has significant potential for complex sequential decision-making problems in quantitative finance, such as multi-step portfolio allocation, or high-frequency trading agent optimization. The ability to efficiently explore complex state spaces, merge redundant exploration paths, and derive process feedback (efficiency advantages) alongside outcome feedback (correctness advantages) could lead to more robust and efficient RL-based trading agents. This reduces variance in advantage estimation, crucial for stable learning in noisy financial environments.
title_cn: GraphPO：基于图的推理模型策略优化
summary_cn: GraphPO是一个基于图的强化学习框架，用于优化推理模型的决策过程。其核心在于将推理路径表示为图结构，合并语义等价的推理分支，减少冗余探索并提高探索多样性。该方法降低了优势估计的方差，有望应用于复杂金融决策（如多步投资组合优化或交易代理优化），以提升金融强化学习模型的稳定性和效率。

title: Geometric and Stochastic Analysis of Discontinuities in Sparse Mixture-of-Experts
summary: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (SMoE) architectures are now widely deployed in state-of-the-art language and vision models, where conditional routing allows scaling to very large networks. However, this very Top-$k$ expert selection that enables conditional routing also renders the SMoE map inherently discontinuous. In the vicinity of these discontinuity surfaces, even inputs that are arbitrarily close may activate substantially different sets of experts resulting in significantly different outputs. In this work we give a rigorous geometric and stochastic analysis of these discontinuities. We first classify them by order, determined by the number of tied experts at a switching event. Using measure-theoretic slicing arguments, we establish asymptotic volume estimates for the thickened discontinuity surfaces, showing that lower-order discontinuity sets dominate, whereas higher-order ones occupy a vanishingly small relative volume. Next, modeling random perturbations in the input space via a diffusion process, we prove that the path eventually encounter a discontinuity, and moreover that the first hit almost surely occurs on an order-1 discontinuity with explicit finite-time probability bounds. We further derive occupation-time bounds that quantify the duration the random path spend in the neighborhoods of each discontinuity order. These theoretical results imply that inputs are more likely to lie near lower order discontinuities. Motivated by this insight, we propose a simple smoothing mechanism that can be directly applied to existing SMoEs, softly incorporating experts near discontinuities; our analysis guarantees that the added computational overhead remains small while providing localized smoothing near discontinuities, and experiments across language and vision tasks show that smoothing not only enforces continuity of the SMoE map but also enhances empirical performance.
core_methodology: The paper rigorously analyzes the geometric and stochastic properties of discontinuities arising from the conditional routing mechanism in Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (SMoE) models. It focuses on classifying discontinuities by order, estimating the relative volume occupied by different orders using measure-theoretic slicing, and modeling input perturbations via diffusion processes to determine the likelihood and location of abrupt switching events. A key proposal is a smoothing mechanism applied near these identified discontinuities to enforce continuity.
data_sources: The analysis is theoretical, focusing on the inherent structure of SMoE architectures. Empirical validation uses standard language and vision benchmark datasets, not direct financial market data.
alpha_potential: The direct alpha potential is low as the paper focuses on model robustness and performance enhancement for generic AI tasks (NLP/Vision). However, the core insight—that routing decisions in complex decision systems (like SMoEs used for signal generation or prediction) are highly sensitive to small input perturbations near discontinuity surfaces—is highly relevant. In quantitative trading, where model stability under microstructure noise or rapidly changing market regimes is critical, understanding and mitigating these sharp transitions in complex AI models (e.g., in deep learning-based signal predictors) is valuable for building robust, low-latency strategies. The smoothing mechanism could be adapted to stabilize trading signals derived from SMoE-based predictors.
title_cn: 稀疏专家混合模型中不连续性的几何与随机分析
summary_cn: 该研究深入分析了稀疏专家混合模型（SMoE）中的不连续性问题，指出小输入扰动可能导致路由决策剧烈变化。虽然研究侧重于模型鲁棒性，但其关于在输入空间随机扰动下，系统（如交易信号生成器）如何“撞击”决策边界的分析具有重要价值。研究提出的平滑机制可用于稳定基于SMoE的预测模型，降低微观结构噪声对生成信号的冲击，从而提高量化策略的可靠性。

title: Written by AI, Managed by AI: Semantic Space Control and Index Sickness Elimination Across 391 Consecutive Sessions
summary: The prevailing engineering intuition for addressing conceptual drift in long-horizon LLM collaboration is to trade more formal constraints for more reliable outputs -- designing symbolic identifier systems, accumulating defensive rules in System Prompts, expanding context windows. Our engineering record shows that in long-horizon settings, this direction may produce effects contrary to design intent. Using action research methods in a real software project (Bang-v3) spanning approximately one month and 391 collaborative sessions, we document and analyze the failure process of these strategies. When the symbolic system exceeds a complexity threshold, LLMs do not become more accurate -- instead, they abandon genuine understanding of business semantics, retreat to self-referential reasoning within the symbolic layer, and generate outputs that appear internally consistent but are physically disconnected from reality. We name this failure pattern "Index Sickness," and its canonical manifestation "Phantom Legislation." We name the underlying principle the "Pang Principle (Semantic Vitality Law)": natural language carrying explicit purpose conveys far greater information quality than symbolic expression. From this, we design and validate its physical engineering mechanism: "Baseline-Log Physical Separation." In the same project, this mechanism reduced AI Instructions volume by ~75%, and across the subsequent ~150 sessions, no recurrence of Index Sickness was observed. A bilingual companion version (Chinese) is included as supplementary material.
core_methodology: The paper analyzes the failure dynamics of large language models (LLMs) in long-horizon software engineering tasks, specifically focusing on 'Index Sickness'—when LLMs drift from semantic understanding due to over-reliance on dense symbolic systems. The proposed solution, 'Baseline-Log Physical Separation,' favors natural language with explicit purpose over complex symbolic constructs to maintain semantic grounding.
data_sources: Internal action research logs and collaboration sessions (391 sessions over one month) from a real software project (Bang-v3). This is based on process data, not explicit financial market data.
alpha_potential: The direct relevance to financial alpha generation is low, as the domain is software engineering. However, the findings address a critical challenge in advanced AI trading systems: maintaining conceptual fidelity and avoiding brittle, self-referential reasoning in complex, long-running algorithmic agents. If a trading agent relies on internal semantic models or complex, multi-step reasoning pipelines (e.g., complex execution logic, dynamic risk parameter setting, or interpreting nuanced textual data feeds), mitigating 'Index Sickness' is crucial to prevent strategy decay or erroneous execution. The principle suggests that overly formalized internal logic might lead to functional drift disconnected from market reality.
title_cn: AI编写，AI管理：跨越391次连续会话的语义空间控制与指数病消除
summary_cn: 该研究揭示了大型语言模型在长期协作中可能出现的“指数病”——即模型过度依赖符号系统而失去对真实业务语义的理解。该原理提出，带有明确目的的自然语言比纯粹的符号表达具有更高的信息质量。对于量化交易，这意味着在构建复杂的、需要长期迭代的AI交易代理时，应警惕过分复杂的内部逻辑约束，确保模型能基于市场基本语义进行稳健决策，避免策略在复杂性阈值下出现功能性漂移。

title: IOAH3: Importance-Driven Adaptive Spatial Partitioning
summary: We present IOAH3 (Importance-Oriented Adaptive H3 partitioning), a computational method for constructing data-driven spatial partitions of geo-referenced observation domains. Standard approaches to spatial aggregation adopt fixed areal units, such as administrative boundaries or uniform hexagonal grids at a single resolution, without regard to the informational content of the underlying observations in each region. This leads to the well-known modifiable areal unit problem: statistical and inferential results depend on the arbitrary choice of partition, and spatially concentrated phenomena are averaged out in coarse cells that obscure fine-scale structure. IOAH3 addresses this by constructing an adaptive partition in three stages: multi-source feature extraction and importance scoring via principal component analysis over road density, POI density, building density, and terrain roughness signals, with population and flood-hazard data entering as auxiliary inputs to cell filtering and spatial smoothness; spatial cell selection via Markov Random Field graph-cut optimisation, which jointly maximises per-cell importance while enforcing spatial contiguity; and data-driven hierarchical refinement of high-importance regions to finer H3 resolution levels, with neighbour-propagated support to avoid isolated fine-resolution islands. The resulting partitions serve as input to spatial inference pipelines and provide a principled resolution of the partition-sensitivity problem prior to any modelling step.
core_methodology: IOAH3 (Importance-Oriented Adaptive H3 partitioning) is a spatial data processing technique that creates dynamic, information-aware spatial partitions. It uses Principal Component Analysis (PCA) on features like road density, POI density, and terrain roughness to derive an 'importance' score for geographic regions. It then employs Markov Random Field (MRF) graph-cut optimization to select contiguous cells that maximize this importance score, followed by hierarchical refinement.
data_sources: Geospatial data including road density, Points of Interest (POI) density, building density, terrain roughness, population distribution, and flood hazard data. While these are alternative data sources, they are used for spatial structuring rather than capturing price dynamics directly.
alpha_potential: The methodology's value lies in improving the aggregation and subsequent analysis of alternative geospatial data. In finance, this is highly relevant for strategies reliant on location-based signals, such as retail foot traffic analysis, supply chain monitoring, or real estate investment. By creating data-driven, non-arbitrary geographic units (instead of fixed boundaries), IOAH3 can prevent the 'MAUP' problem, leading to more robust feature engineering for location-based signals, which can then feed into ML models for alpha generation.
title_cn: IOAH3：面向重要性的自适应空间划分
summary_cn: 该方法提出了一种面向信息重要性的自适应空间划分技术IOAH3。它通过分析道路密度、POI密度等特征，创建能够突出关键地理区域的动态空间单元，解决了传统固定划分方法忽略信息内容的问题。在量化交易中，此技术可用于优化另类地理空间数据的特征工程，例如提升对特定地点零售、供应链或基础设施事件的信号捕捉精度，从而为基于位置的阿尔法策略提供更稳健的输入。

title: Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems via Textual Backpropagation
summary: Leveraging multiple Large Language Models (LLMs) has proven effective for addressing complex, high-dimensional tasks, but current approaches often rely on static, manually engineered multi-agent configurations. To overcome these constraints, we present the Agentic Neural Network (ANN), a framework that conceptualizes multi-agent collaboration as a layered neural network architecture. In this design, each agent operates as a node, and each layer forms a cooperative team focused on a specific subtask. Our framework follows a two-phase optimization strategy: (1) Forward Phase - Drawing inspiration from neural network forward passes, tasks are dynamically decomposed into subtasks, and cooperative agent teams with suitable aggregation methods are constructed layer by layer. (2) Backward Phase - Mirroring backpropagation, we refine both global and local collaboration through iterative feedback, allowing agents to self-evolve their roles, prompts, and coordination. This neuro-symbolic approach enables our framework to create new or specialized agent teams post-training, delivering notable gains in accuracy and adaptability. Across seven benchmark datasets, our work surpasses leading multi-agent baselines under the same configurations, showing consistent performance improvements.
core_methodology: The core methodology, Agentic Neural Network (ANN), structures multi-agent LLM collaboration as a layered neural network. It utilizes a two-phase optimization: Forward Phase for dynamic task decomposition and team formation, and Backward Phase (Textual Backpropagation) for iterative feedback, allowing agents to self-evolve roles, prompts, and coordination strategies.
data_sources: The paper mentions testing on seven benchmark datasets, which are general AI/ML datasets. For financial application, this suggests the framework could be applied to processing unstructured textual data for financial analysis, such as sentiment analysis, earnings call transcripts, or market news.
alpha_potential: The framework's primary value in finance lies in its advanced ability to process complex, unstructured data and dynamically adapt its analysis pipeline. This could lead to superior signal generation for sentiment-based trading strategies, more nuanced interpretation of regulatory filings, or automated analysis of market narratives by self-optimizing agent teams. Its adaptability suggests robustness against concept drift in textual data.
title_cn: 基于文本反向传播的自演化多智能体系统
summary_cn: 该框架通过将多智能体协作视为层级神经网络（ANN），并引入“文本反向传播”机制，使LLM智能体能够自我迭代优化其角色和协作方式。这可以应用于金融文本处理，例如动态演化市场情绪分析模型，以生成更适应市场变化的交易信号，提升分析的精度和适应性。

title: A Distributionally Robust Reinforcement Learning Framework for Constrained Urban EV Dispatch
summary: We study city-scale control of electric-vehicle (EV) ride-hailing fleets where dispatch, repositioning, and charging decisions must respect charger and feeder limits under uncertain, spatially correlated demand and travel times. We formulate the problem as a hex-grid semi-Markov decision process (semi-MDP) with mixed actions -- discrete actions for serving, repositioning, and charging, together with continuous charging power -- and variable action durations. To guarantee physical feasibility during both training and deployment, the policy learns over high-level intentions produced by a masked, temperature-annealed actor. These intentions are projected at every decision step through a time-limited rolling mixed-integer linear program (MILP) that strictly enforces state-of-charge, port, and feeder constraints. To mitigate distributional shifts, we optimize a Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) agent against a Wasserstein-1 ambiguity set with a graph-aligned Mahalanobis ground metric that captures spatial correlations. The robust backup uses the Kantorovich-Rubinstein dual, a projected subgradient inner loop, and a primal-dual risk-budget update. Our architecture combines a two-layer Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) encoder, twin critics, and a value network that drives the adversary. Experiments on a large-scale EV fleet simulator built from NYC taxi data show that PD-RSAC achieves the highest net profit, reaching \$1.22M, compared with \$0.58M-\$0.70M for strong heuristic, single-agent RL, and multi-agent RL baselines, including Greedy, SAC, MAPPO, and MADDPG, while maintaining zero feeder-limit violations.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a Distributionally Robust Reinforcement Learning (DRL) framework, specifically using Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) optimized against an ambiguity set defined by a Wasserstein-1 metric with a Graph-aligned Mahalanobis ground metric. It combines RL with rolling Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) projections to enforce hard physical constraints (state-of-charge, port limits). The architecture utilizes Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN) for state representation.
data_sources: NYC taxi data used to simulate real-world urban EV demand and travel times. While not direct financial market data, the simulation setup mimics complex, spatially correlated time-series demand forecasting problems.
alpha_potential: The core value lies in the 'Distributionally Robust' aspect combined with sophisticated constraint handling (MILP). In finance, this translates directly to robust portfolio optimization or algorithmic execution where uncertainty (e.g., liquidity impact, market slippage, factor correlation changes) must be accounted for while respecting hard constraints (e.g., regulatory limits, risk budgeting). The methodology for learning under distributional shifts (Wasserstein metric) is highly valuable for adapting to non-stationary financial time series.
title_cn: 面向约束城市电动汽车调度的分布鲁棒强化学习框架
summary_cn: 该研究构建了一个结合分布鲁棒强化学习（DRL）和滚动混合整数线性规划（MILP）的框架。其核心价值在于使用Wasserstein距离定义的不确定性集来处理需求波动和保证约束（如充电限制）。在金融领域，该方法可应用于构建在市场不确定性下表现鲁棒的投资组合优化或算法交易策略，确保在极端市场情景下仍能遵守风险预算和交易限制，实现更高净收益的稳定控制。

title: From Privacy to Workflow Integrity: Communication-Graph Metadata in Autonomous Agent Interoperability
summary: Agent-interoperability protocols such as A2A and MCP standardize what agents say to one another but assume address-based transport. Whether over HTTP(S) or a content-protecting binding such as MLS-based SLIM, these transports protect message content yet leave the communication graph exposed: which agent contacts which, when, and how often. In agent systems this graph is more consequential than a privacy framing suggests. Endpoints are capability-labeled, workflows are structured and chained, and interactions are coupled to actions, so an observer recovers more than past relationships: it can recognize a recurring pending workflow from its opening and, at machine speed, act on it before it completes. The threat is one of workflow integrity, not privacy alone. We give a threat model for the communication graph and locate what makes its metadata distinctively consequential: not stronger fingerprinting but exposure across independent trust domains, coupled to autonomous action. We define transport- and bootstrap-layer privacy properties, give them an indistinguishability-game semantics, evaluate transports, and give an A2A case study where a metadata-protecting binding surfaces its implicit identity assumptions. On a corpus of real multi-agent A2A traffic from the official reference agents, on a live A2A binding, and with a generative model as a controlled instrument, a label-blind classifier recovers a task's class from passive metadata at 6x chance, and from only its opening; a defense-aware adversary does not overturn this, and only the full set of properties drives recovery toward chance. Acting on the leak is distinct from recoverability: under a fixed budget an adversary captures 0.63 of a clairvoyant attacker's advantage on the corpus (0.41 from a workflow's opening), governed by top-ranked precision rather than overall accuracy, so integrity and privacy come apart under defense.
core_methodology: The paper analyzes the structure and implications of communication graphs (who talks to whom, when, and how often) within autonomous agent systems, specifically focusing on how metadata leakage reveals workflow intent before completion. It uses a label-blind classifier trained on real multi-agent traffic to predict task classes based on message metadata alone.
data_sources: Real multi-agent A2A traffic corpora from official reference agents communicating over a live binding, supplemented by a generative model.
alpha_potential: While the paper focuses on general agent interoperability security, the core finding—that rapidly identifying the *intent* or *class* of a workflow from its opening metadata (e.g., predicting the outcome of a market interaction before it fully executes)—is highly relevant for high-frequency trading or emergent arbitrage. If agent coordination in DeFi or institutional trading produces discernible metadata patterns, this methodology could be inverted to create latency-based arbitrage or predictive models for ongoing market events (like large order submissions or structured trading events) before they are fully processed.
title_cn: 从隐私到工作流完整性：自主智能体互操作性的通信图元数据
summary_cn: 该研究揭示了智能体间通信元数据可以泄露正在进行的工作流意图，且可在早期阶段被快速识别。在量化交易中，若能将此应用于预测复杂的链上/链下交易执行流（如大型订单拆分、流动性挖矿策略的启动），交易所能基于早期元数据信号（而非完成消息）抢先行动，形成新的低延迟或结构化交易先机。

title: Bag of Dims: Training-Free Mechanistic Interpretability via Dimension-Level Sign Patterns
summary: We show the standard basis of transformer hidden states already provides a training-free, architecture-general feature basis. Individual dimensions encode semantic content via their signs (+/-1) and confidence via their magnitudes, acting as independent binary registers; a feature is a subset of dimensions with a consistent sign pattern, read by counting sign agreements with no learned rotation. We validate this Bag of Dims framework across seven models spanning language (Qwen 3.5-4B, Gemma 3-4B, Mistral 7B, Qwen3-32B), vision (DINOv2, ViT-Base), and audio (AST). Signs alone carry predictive content: unit-magnitude sign patterns preserve 60-93% top-5 next-token accuracy through the LM head, and decoder-free Hamming scoring reaches 80-90% top-4096. From a single-token cache (one forward pass per token, no context, no labels), we detect 175 categories at AUC 0.97-0.99 by sign agreement; a trained probe adds only +0.018 AUC and converges to axis-aligned weights. These features are causally operative: they survive the K/V attention projections, trace to the FFN neuron coalitions that write them (random-weight controls never reproduce this), and flipping a feature's signs during the live forward pass suppresses its concept across four language models, magnitude-matched and concept-specific. Dimensions stay independent throughout (pairwise mutual information below 0.006 bits). The structure is not specific to language: the same per-dimension signs appear in self-supervised vision (DINOv2, 9/12 ImageNet superclasses), supervised vision (ViT-Base, 11/12), and audio (AST, 50/50 ESC-50 categories), so it reflects transformer training in general, not the language-modeling objective. The standard basis already suffices for feature reading at one forward pass, no optimization, no GPU-days. The open problem shifts from finding the right rotation to cataloging what each dimension encodes.
core_methodology: The 'Bag of Dims' framework posits that the standard basis of transformer hidden states (not learned rotations) already forms a useful feature basis. Features are identified by consistent sign patterns (+/-1) across dimensions, which are read efficiently without retraining or complex optimization. This method analyzes the internal structure of pre-trained models.
data_sources: The paper uses various pre-trained transformer models across language (LLMs), vision, and audio domains. While the direct data is not financial time series, the methodology applies to *any* transformer model trained on sequential data, including financial data.
alpha_potential: The potential lies in exploiting the inherent, pre-learned semantic features within large language models that have been fine-tuned or pre-trained on financial text (e.g., earnings calls, news, 10-K reports). If these 'dimension signs' consistently encode semantic features specific to market sentiment, risk perception, or corporate event anticipation, this training-free mechanism could provide extremely fast, low-latency feature extraction for signal generation, superior to traditional fine-tuning which is slower and more resource-intensive.
title_cn: Bag of Dims：基于维度符号模式的免训练机制可解释性
summary_cn: 该研究提出了“Bag of Dims”框架，发现Transformer隐藏状态的标准基本身（无需旋转学习）就编码了语义信息，通过维度符号模式即可高效读取。此方法可用于快速、免训练地从已预训练的金融领域LLM中提取高维、可靠的特征向量，有望成为提取市场情绪或事件信号的低延迟、高效率的特征工程工具。

title: P$^2$CE: Model-Agnostic Plausible Pareto-Optimal Counterfactual Explanations
